comments.author: ajayyy
comments.textRawHtml:
I recently did a talk in opposition of this sentiment

Yes, some projects like stack overflow may be losing contributors by a large degree, but it doesn't have to be this way

I run SponsorBlock and DeArrow which are two human powered crowdsourced browser extensions that are only growing in scale in opposition to the want to slopify everything

We have 17% of submitters every week being first time contributors and 19% being old, a nice balance.

Unfortunately the talk isn't available yet but you can see the slides here https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1nGArM7c3i9cVGGvkh6ER...

children.author: goodmythical
children.textRawHtml:
>SponsorBlock

I am routinely amazed at the speed and breadth of the SponsorBlock community.

Popular channels are tagged within minutes of posting. Obscure channels almost always get tags at some point.

The only place I've noticed significant lack of coverage is really long older videos, like say MIT OpenCourseWare. Not a complaint at all, not expecting anyone to sit through hundreds of hours of college to mark up a few tangents here and there, just an observation.

children.author: chrismorgan
children.textRawHtml:
> We have 17% of submitters every week being first time contributors

That doesn’t sound like necessarily a positive thing; it sounds like it could well be unsustainable churn (impossible to tell from such limited numbers, I don’t know what the general growth figures are or proportional trends).

I have contributed in the past, but don’t any more because of how you went out of your way to make it tedious: https://github.com/ajayyy/SponsorBlock/issues/2106. I suspect there are a lot more that have been driven away by the unnecessary and not even accurate mandatory preview step.

children.author: goodmythical
children.textRawHtml:
Any are welcome, so far as I know having not checked their submission criteria, to spin it up and contribute tags to the SponsorBlock community. I'd wager there are people already doing so.

I think it would be more useful to more people to utilize the existing solution because it runs in a very small footprint for the end user. Most people wouldn't be able to run an entire TTS/LLM workflow without processing videos in the background or waiting some multiple of real-time in order to watch a video.

You could maybe do it with just LLM tagging the transcript, but that's still a ton of processing just to watch a video.

God that'd be so much wasted energy if every person wanting to skip in-video ads was running an entire LLM to do so.

children.author: maxglute
children.textRawHtml:
Unavoidable for some stuff like podcasts where they inject random sponsorship into audio files and throws off all the timestamps. Though maybe wasteful llm adblock compute breaks ad serving compute, they somehow cancel each other out by making all the compute wasted on ads + telemetry defunct.

Circle back to original topic, eventually having local LLMs intercepting EVERYTHING in background to reproject a curated personal bubble filter feels like wasteful but sensible end game. Not just to hide ads / skip sponsors, run every image through anime filter, live editing xyz, if there'es some centralized DB to grab timestamps do it, but otherwise we could be burning tokens none stop to modify reality, and some add manipulation is just rounding error that comes along for the ride. I click a video, background processes play opens 10 instances of the video at 4x speed, processes, gives me version of video without ads, sponsorblocs, xyz content filtered out... or just generate video to conform to my biases because it makes me feel good.

children.author: banana_giraffe
children.textRawHtml:
It's not sponsorblock quality, but I have trained a model for podcasts. Turns out, at least for podcasts, you can get away with a surprisingly small model, small enough it can run on device directly.

No idea if it's good enough for all podcasts that are out there. It works for me and the podcasts I listen to, and I have tried testing it against a larger corpus, but I'm one developer and I just wanted to solve a problem for me.

https://github.com/Q726kbXuN/podcast-ad-tagger
